Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • pyproject.toml uses the standard setuptools.build_meta backend; the provided content shows no custom build hook intended for arbitrary install-time execution.
  • setup.cfg only contains [egg_info] settings and no executable logic.
  • No evidence was provided for .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, install/interpreter-start execution, or suspicious import-time side effects.
  • The GitHub Actions and deployment workflows appear to be normal repository CI/CD behavior, not an automatic malicious execution path in the package installer’s environment.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • Credential theft: No evidence of broad environment-variable harvesting, .env discovery, SSH key collection, cloud/CI token discovery, wallet theft, or registry-token harvesting. The GRAPHDB_* environment variables appear to be normal GraphDB connection configuration and are not tied to malicious collection.
  • Exfiltration/upload: The httpx.post/put/get/delete calls in src/cimsparql/graphdb.py are consistent with a GraphDB/RDF4J/Blazegraph client uploading and querying RDF/SPARQL data to user-configured services. There is no evidence of sensitive-data collection followed by upload to an attacker-controlled endpoint.
  • Archive staging: The .zip string in tests/data/micro/README.md is a test-model source filename reference, not evidence of file harvesting, compression, or staging logic.
  • Persistence: No cron, systemd, launch agent, shell-profile modification, background polling loop, or self-reinstall logic was identified.
  • Lateral movement: No evidence of Kubernetes token usage, Docker socket access, cloud metadata access, GitHub Actions workflow injection, or CI token reuse for lateral movement.
  • Obfuscation/loader behavior: Use of re.compile(...) is ordinary parsing logic in test utilities. No evidence of eval/exec, base64/zlib/marshal loaders, obfuscated downloader stubs, or staged payload loading was identified.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • The sdist includes hidden paths such as .github, .pre-commit-config.yaml, and .gitignore, but they are listed in SOURCES.txt and appear to be ordinary project/CI configuration files. No executable payload or malicious supply-chain behavior is evident from them.
  • Dependencies in pyproject.toml and requires.txt appear consistent within the provided material; no evidence of suspicious sudden dependency insertion or typosquatting was identified.
  • No evidence was provided for unexplained native binaries, hidden payloads, abnormal egg-info/dist-info contents, or wheel/sdist behavior mismatch.

Additional Verification Needed

  • The input is focused on selected file text; all 145 files, large XML/data files, and any potential binary content were not fully reviewed.
  • The provided artifact is an sdist (.tar.gz). If a wheel exists, compare wheel and sdist contents and execution paths for discrepancies.
